content:
Sam Green: Heads up — large p95 spike on pool-gamma starting ~03:14 UTC. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~380ms for short-text workloads (seq<=64). Any recent changes?

Deploy Bot: deploy-bot: rolled runtime v2.14 to pool-gamma @ 03:10 UTC — selector now prefers fused_int8_attention when beneficial.

Olivia Kim: That matches the timeline. I pushed a kernel-selector tweak this morning to prefer fused_int8 for >32 tokens to improve throughput in our bench. Maybe threshold is too aggressive for real traffic.

Matt Johnson: Captured a perf snapshot — KV cache eviction rate spiked around the same time, batch sizes collapsed and queue depth increased. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/pool-gamma/overview?ts=1795601200

Ryan Infra: pprof from a worker at 03:16: 
```text
fused_attn_int8     45.2%
memcpy_h2d          29.3%
kernel_launch       12.1%
other_kernels       13.4%
```
NVTX timeline shows a lot of short kernels w/ high launch overhead — the launch/memcopy cost is dominating for short sequences.

Nina Patel: Tenant org-72 sent a burst of tiny requests at 03:12 (cold-start fanout). They were on shared pool-gamma with high concurrency; backpressure plus selector choosing int8 for short seqs looks like the perfect storm.

Olivia Kim: Immediate plan: rollback selector change on pool-gamma, and push a quick safeguard to prefer fp16 for seq < 48. Also add per-tenant in-flight caps. I'll open a PR now.

Sam Green: Can infra throttle org-72 while we fix the selector? We should limit blast radius.

Ryan Infra: Added a soft in-flight cap for org-72 (32 -> 8) on prod. Monitoring latency and queue length.

Deploy Bot: deploy-bot: rollback runtime selector on pool-gamma to v2.13 initiated by Olivia Kim @ 03:26 UTC.

Matt Johnson: Post-rollback p95 dropped to ~140ms within two cycles and KV eviction rate fell. Looks promising. Will keep an eye for 30m.

Nina Patel: :thumbsup: I'll reach out to the tenant team to discuss rate limits and recommend Dedicated if their pattern persists.

Olivia Kim: Follow-ups (will file tickets): [1] refine kernel-selector heuristics to include seq-length heuristics and batching overhead model; [2] auto-fallback when kernel-launch penalty exceeds threshold for observed seq distribution; [3] enforce per-tenant queue depth at the runtime router level.

Sam Green: Thanks all. Marking this resolved for now — re-open if spikes recur in next 30m.

Ryan Infra: attaching minimal logs and worker pprof here for postmortem (link): https://logs.redwood/pool-gamma/1795601200-1795601400

Olivia Kim: I'll prepare a short postmortem and a short-lived metric alert for 'kernel_launch_pct > 20% for short-seq traffic' to catch regressions.

Matt Johnson: Nice catch — good outcome from quick rollback + tenant cap.
